_strings.@@0dbc7e66bc7a: Ohio Earned Income Credit (EIC) — Taxpayers who qualified for and claimed the federal Earned Income Tax Credit for tax year 2025 (federal Form 1040/1040-SR, line 27a). Eligibility tracks the federal EIC.
_strings.@@1b090f3f0709: Print only the form pages (not instructions), single-sided; attach state copies of W-2/1099.
_strings.@@1b0f97dd7fa7: Treaty conformity — OH conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from OH income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the OH return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Ohio IT 1040 line 1 starts from federal adjusted gross income (2025 form line 1: "Federal adjusted gross income (federal 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11a)"). Ohio AGI = line 1 + additions (Ohio Schedule of Adjustments, line 12) - deductions (line 47). The 2025 Schedule of Adjustments additions list (non-Ohio state or local government interest and dividends; pass-through entity add-back; taxes paid to another state or D.C. related to IRS notice 2020-75; 529 plan funds used for non-qualified expenses; losses from sale or disposition of Ohio public obligations; nonmedical withdrawals from a medical savings account; reimbursement of expenses previously deducted on an Ohio return; Ohio Homebuyer Plus non-eligible withdrawals; IRC 168(k)/179 depreciation add-back; federally exempt U.S. obligation interest taxable by the state; federal conformity additions) contains NO add-back of federally treaty-exempt income. Therefore income excluded from federal AGI under a U.S. tax treaty flows through and is not re-taxed by Ohio. Federal-AGI common case, no treaty addback -> conforms.
_strings.@@1b3aafe722c0: Exemption Credit — Taxpayers whose modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) less exemptions is less than $30,000.
_strings.@@26b13913b234: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): NEW high-income cutoff in the personal/dependent exemption table for 2025: the table gained a FOURTH tier of $0 per exemption once modified adjusted gross income is $750,000 or greater (booklet p. 17: $2,400 at MAGI $40,000 or less; $2,150 at $40,001-$80,000; $1,900 at $80,001-$749,999; $0 at $750,000 or more). The 2024 table had NO upper cutoff — its $1,900 tier ran to infinity — so a high-income 2025 filer now gets no exemption at all on IT 1040 line 4. This is a structural cutoff, not the annual re-tiering of the amounts (the $2,400 / $2,150 / $1,900 figures themselves are unchanged from 2024). Resolve via: 2025 Ohio IT 1040 / SD 100 Instruction Booklet p. 17 personal and dependent exemption table (the citation URL) plus the MAGI worksheet referenced on booklet p. 40 (MAGI = Ohio adjusted gross income plus the business income deduction, R.C. 5747.01(II)); this pack ships no exemptions because the amount depends on income.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: IT 1040 line 8a: 'Nonbusiness income tax liability on line 7a (see tax.ohio.gov/taxcalculator or see the instructions for the tax brackets)'. Booklet p. 18 table headings: 'Taxable Nonbusiness Income (Ohio IT 1040, line 7)' -> 'Nonbusiness Income Tax (enter on Ohio IT 1040, line 8a)'. Line 8c 'Income tax liability before credits (line 8a plus line 8b)' adds the separate 3% business income tax (line 8b), which this op does not model. This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: 2025 CHANGE — TOP RATE CUT TO 3.125%, STRUCTURE STILL THREE ROWS: 'Ohio Income Tax Brackets. For tax year 2025, the highest tax rate has been reduced to 3.125%' (Highlights for Tax Year 2025). The 2025 schedule (booklet p. 18) is 0.000% for 0 to $26,050, then 2.750% to $100,000, then 3.125% over $100,000. Ohio did NOT consolidate to a single rate for 2025 — do not use the 2024 3.50% top rate, and do not flatten. R.C. 5747.02(A)(3)(c) shows the consolidation arrives NEXT year: 'For taxable years beginning in 2026 and thereafter, $332.00 plus 2.75% of the amount in excess of $26,050' — a single rate above the zero bracket. That 2026 schedule must not be applied to 2025. Base guidance: Supply 2025 Ohio IT 1040 line 7 (= line 7a), 'Taxable nonbusiness income (line 5 minus line 6; if negative, enter zero)'.
